settings.name: Bellamy Salvage Yard
settings.description: A sprawling lot of rusted metal and silence, smelling of ozone and wet iron, where the Ohio River fog settles thick against the chain-link fence.

settings.name: First Presbyterian Church Parsonage
settings.description: A drafty Victorian house with peeling paint, smelling of stale coffee and lemon polish, where shadows stretch long across the hardwood floors.

settings.name: Ruth Hollister’s Apartment
settings.description: A cramped second-floor flat in Weirton, cluttered with card tables and empty pill bottles, smelling of mothballs and burnt toast.

settings.name: The Ohio River Bank
settings.description: A muddy, sludge-stained edge of water, smelling of diesel and decay, where barges move slowly like sleeping beasts.

plot_points.description: Wally finds the dented brass jewelry box in the crusher feed; he pulls it out just before the blades engage, recognizing the initials "JB → EL".
Danny arrests a local man for DUI, refusing to let him go despite the man’s connection to the Sheriff’s donor list, showing Danny’s rigid integrity.
Wally meets Ruth Hollister; she reveals her husband bought the box in 1988 from a man who claimed it was "junk," but Ruth suspects otherwise.
Wally realizes the "boyfriend" Janine mentioned was John Hollister, Ruth’s stepson, not a stranger; the killer is within the community, not a transient trucker.
Salvador dies in the yard office; Wally breaks down, realizing his investigation was a way to avoid grieving Eileen, and now he must face both losses.
Wally confronts Dean in the parsonage; Dean admits he knew John killed Janine but stayed silent to protect his marriage and the church’s stability.

voice: Third-person limited, past tense, restrained and tactile, focusing on the physical weight of objects and the quiet erosion of time.
